original_evidence_excerpt: The cart struck the first employee in the torso area and pinned him underneath.
correction_reason: A manually pushed cart is not an IOGP driving event.
narrative: On or about March 10, 2015, at 2:30 p.m., two employees got struck by a drilling motor and a cart. While pushing the cart from the outside of the building to the inside, the cart tipped and the drilling motor fell off. The cart struck the first employee in the torso area and pinned him underneath. The cart struck the second employee when it tipped and propelled to the side. The second employee sustained a forehead contusion, fractured left ankle, right ear laceration, and fractured facial bone. Both employees were taken to the hospital.

narrative: An employee was loading equipment and tools onto a truck to prepare to leave a well site. The employee was standing on a lubricator rack/catwalk where he was releasing the straps on the crane when the catwalk collapsed. The employee fell approximately 5 feet to the truck below and hit his head. He was hospitalized.

original_evidence_excerpt: The employee's momentum carried him approximately 6 feet further where he struck his left shoulder on a decorative concrete wall and then fell.
correction_reason: The phrase 'guy wire directly ... struck' triggered the pattern; no vehicle or driving is described.
narrative: An employee was pulling on a tree limb located on the ground using a 6-foot long hanger puller. When the hanger puller became dislodged from the limb, the employee tripped over an anchored guy wire directly behind him. The employee's momentum carried him approximately 6 feet further where he struck his left shoulder on a decorative concrete wall and then fell. The employee sustained fractures to the right fibula, ankle, and left shoulder.

original_evidence_excerpt: While the excavator was pulling the auger, the chain failed and whiplashed into the employee's face.
correction_reason: A chain failure does not establish a permit or work-authorisation requirement.
narrative: An employee was standing next to a bore pipe observing the work. An excavator was being used to pull an auger bit out of the bore pipe. A chain was attached to the excavator to pull the auger sections. While the excavator was pulling the auger, the chain failed and whiplashed into the employee's face. The employee lost the left eye and suffered a right orbital socket fracture.
